blocks: This unit genuinely has an MCU that measures things — four temperature sensors, supply voltage, door state, compressor faults — and it renders all of it on a front display panel. What is missing is any way off the appliance. 325L_DC_fridge_EN_manual_June2024.pdf's component list is: 1 Fuse 30A, 2 Driver Board, 3 Compressor Grounding, 4 Fuse 10A, 5 Frosting Heater, 6 Fan, 7 Damper, 8 Main Control Board, 9 Display Panel, 10 Fridge LED Light, 11 Lamp Light, 12 No Frost Sensor, 13 Freezer Sensor, 14 Fridge Sensor, 15 Ambient Sensor. No connector, terminal, or port appears anywhere in that list or in the wiring section, and the same comms grep (modbus / rs-485 / CAN / bluetooth / wi-fi / ethernet / USB / app) returns zero hits across the whole document. What blocks a driver is therefore a hardware gap, not a documentation gap, and no amount of further research closes it — only a teardown would.

unmappedReports: Fault / error code. The panel emits E1 ambient sensor failure, E2 fridge sensor failure, E3 freezer sensor failure, E4 frosting sensor failure, HI over-voltage, LO under-voltage, Ed door not closed, EC internal comms failure, E6 fan failure, EP supply over 29 V, E7 compressor failure, E8 compressor start overload, E9 compressor start overheat. MetricKind has no fault-code or alarm-state member at all — the nearest thing in the contract is the CommandKind `clear-fault`, which implies a fault concept the metric vocabulary never defines. Contract gap., Door open state (error Ed and the door-alarm feature). No `door-state` MetricKind. `switch-state` is the only boolean of the right shape and it is semantically wrong — a door is not a switch the system controls., Compressor run state. ValueKind::RunState already exists but the only MetricKind wired to it is `generator-run-state`. There is no `compressor-run-state`, so a fridge cannot report whether it is currently drawing., Temperature setpoints, fridge (+1..+7 C) and freezer (-18..-12 C). MetricKind::Temperature is a measurement; the contract has no setpoint/target concept and no `set-temperature` CommandKind. Both a metric gap and a command gap., Four distinct compartment temperatures — fridge sensor, freezer sensor, ambient sensor, no-frost sensor. MetricKind::Temperature is a single undifferentiated Celsius kind, so four physically different readings from one device would collide on one wire name. Same shape of problem the DS18B20 per-probe device-kind config in local-io.md works around., Under-voltage / over-voltage alarm state as a distinct latched condition, separate from the voltage value itself. No alarm MetricKind exists., NOTE ON ALL OF THE ABOVE: these are displayed on the appliance's own front panel and are not readable over any wire. They are recorded as contract findings — gaps that DeviceKind::Refrigerator will hit the moment any fridge with a real port is catalogued — not as a claim that a driver could obtain them from a UGP-325L.
